name: cancel_execution
description: Request cancellation of an active durable execution by its ID.

name: capture_file
description:
Index a file and return a compact versioned JSON summary.

    Verify the path before reading. Symlinks are followed; pipes and devices are
    rejected. Resolve symlinks when path identity matters, confirm the expected
    workspace, and set max_bytes for large or untrusted files. Capture limits do
    not validate filesystem intent. Optional structured_metrics are retained.

name: capture_text
description:
Ingest already-collected text and return capture metadata.

    Use this when the caller already has output to index. For a noisy or
    potentially long command, use ``execute_and_capture`` so output remains
    bounded before it reaches the agent context. The return value is a compact
    versioned JSON summary; optional named metrics are retained in
    ``structured_metrics``.

name: clear_captures
description: Clears all or a specific capture from the ephemeral buffer to free memory.

name: consolidate_captures
description:
Create one bounded, searchable JSON capture from multiple captures.

    The consolidated capture keeps source capture IDs and source line numbers.
    If records do not fit, the complete source captures remain available through
    their original IDs until normal LRU eviction. The operation fails if the
    consolidated capture cannot be admitted while retaining those sources.

name: execute_and_capture
description:
Run a command and return compact JSON with status, duration, sizes, token
    estimates, truncation, signals, previews, and optional metrics. Log previews
    show bounded head/tail lines. Check them first; preserve requested signals,
    test names, line numbers, and assertion text verbatim. Search for missing
    details and slice only if evidence is absent or truncated.

    Use for commands expected to finish within the MCP client's tool-call window.
    Use start_execution when duration may approach or exceed that window; use
    direct execution for short targeted inspections. Choose by duration independently of output size.

    Verify command, repository, and working directory. Omitted cwd inherits the server process directory.
    Symlinks or shell expansion can target another path; output limits do not ensure filesystem safety.

    Labels default to the command. content_type accepts auto, diff, log, or text.
    max_output_bytes cannot exceed the buffer limit. Timeout retains output and
    returns exit code 124. structured_metrics accepts JSON-compatible named metrics.

name: get_buffer_stats
description: Return aggregate capture, admission, accounting, and process RSS metrics.

name: get_capture_slice
description:
Fetch a byte-bounded page of 1-indexed capture lines.

    Repeat the range and capture ID from the first call, then pass the returned
    opaque ``next_cursor`` to continue. Pages never split a Unicode character;
    the cursor's line offset is a zero-based UTF-8 byte offset.

name: get_capture_summary
description:
Returns a compact versioned JSON summary. Set ``include_previews`` when
    head and tail samples are needed; full output remains available through
    ``get_capture_slice``.

name: get_execution
description: Return durable phase metadata and event history for one execution.

name: get_execution_capacity
description: Report durable storage diagnostics and active/queued background execution counts.

name: get_execution_output
description: Retrieve bounded output; page one phase using UTF-8 byte offsets.

offset.description: UTF-8 byte offset when paging one phase
offset.title: Offset

name: get_runtime_diagnostics
description: Returns opt-in runtime metadata without exposing captured content.

name: get_usage_metrics
description: Return content-free usage metrics, optionally since a snapshot token.

name: list_captures
description:
List active captures with readable text and structured capture data.

    ``limit`` must be 1–25. Pass the opaque ``next_cursor`` to continue a stable
    newest-first snapshot; captures evicted before their page is read are
    omitted. The structured result includes ``page_count`` and the current
    active ``capture_count``.

name: list_executions
description: List durable executions with compact partial/completion summaries.

name: preflight_command
description:
Return content-free path and executable diagnostics without running ``command``.

    This resolves the working directory, symlink target, detectable Git
    repository root, and first executable token. Relative and empty PATH entries
    are resolved against the requested working directory. Shell expansion, aliases,
    pipelines, redirections, environment changes, and arbitrary shell logic
    cannot be verified here. The requested command is never executed.

name: resume_execution
description:
Resume at the first incomplete phase.

    When invoked through MCP, remaining phases run in the background and the
    call returns promptly. Direct Python calls run resumed phases synchronously
    and return after the run completes or encounters a stopping condition.

    Use get_execution for progress; caller disconnection detaches. Completed
    phases are skipped, and safe interrupted phases resume normally. Failed or
    timed-out phases require retry_failed=True. Unsafe retries also require
    confirm_unsafe=True unless the execution used the allow-unsafe policy.

name: retire_executions
description:
Preview selected durable records or archive and retire them.

    A dry run is read-only and reports eligibility and projected space reclaimed.
    Actual retirement requires an archive path outside the state directory; the
    archived bundle is durably written before the source record pair is removed.
    Active and fence-pending executions are never retired.

name: search_capture
description:
Search a capture by query text and return bounded readable and structured matches.

    mode is hybrid (default, lexical and semantic), bm25 (lexical), or semantic
    (embedding based). capture_id defaults to latest; top_k defaults to 5
    (maximum 20), and context_lines defaults to 3 (maximum 100). Use
    get_capture_slice for complete or omitted content.
    `semantic_coverage: complete` means indexed, not every source token was
    embedded. Oversized lines stay whole but the tokenizer may truncate them
    at the model's token limit.

name: set_semantic_index_budget
description: Adjust this session's semantic-index chunk budget when explicitly enabled.

name: start_execution
description:
Start a sequential, durably checkpointed workflow.

    Use for commands likely to approach or exceed the MCP client's tool-call
    window, including one command as one phase, regardless of output size. When
    invoked through MCP, phases run in the background and the call returns an ID
    promptly; use get_execution and get_execution_output to follow work. Direct
    Python calls run phases synchronously and return after the workflow completes
    or encounters a stopping condition.
    Caller disconnection detaches; cancel_execution requests termination.

    Requires Linux process-recovery support and admits eight active or queued
    executions. Check get_execution_capacity before scheduling. Configure
    EPHEMERAL_SESSION_ID, EPHEMERAL_SOCKET_PATH, or
    EPHEMERAL_EXECUTION_STATE_DIR to preserve state across restarts.

    Each phase requires name and command. Completed phases are never rerun.
    Failed or timed-out phases require retry_failed=True. Retrying an unsafe
    phase also requires confirm_unsafe=True unless the execution used
    resume_policy='allow-unsafe'. State uses the session identity or a
    process-private directory by default.
